name: Indian Energy Exchange Ltd
title: Indian Energy Exchange Ltd - 540750 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IEX Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 10.8% YoY to INR 129.8 crore on record 39.4 billion units traded volume.
summary.overview: IEX delivered record quarterly electricity volume of 39.4 billion units (up 24.3% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR 196.4 crore (up 12.5%), with PAT up 10.8% to INR 129.8 crore. Full-year PAT rose 14.9% to INR 492.9 crore and a final dividend of INR 2 per share was declared. Exchange prices fell sharply on higher sell-side liquidity (DAM down 12.2% YoY in Q4), and other income dropped about 29% sequentially-adjusted per analyst, attributed to treasury mark-to-market losses in March. Market coupling (CERC draft of April 17, 2026 naming Grid India as MCO, comments till May 16) is the dominant overhang, with management disputing its benefit. Gas exchange (IGX) volumes fell 8% in Q4 on Middle East supply disruption and management expects no growth in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2 per share (200% of face value)

segments.name: Electricity - DAM/RTM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 DAM price averaged INR 3.89/unit (down 12.2% YoY) and RTM INR 3.68/unit (down 15%) as DAM sell-bids rose about 49%. RTM was 39% of electricity volumes in FY26 (55 billion units, up about 41%).

segments.name: Green market (G-DAM)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 green volume rose 26.5% to 2.4 billion units; FY26 volume 10.8 billion units (+23%).

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 RECs traded 71.7 lakh (+6% YoY); FY26 187 lakh (+5%).

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume down 8% on Middle East supply disruption; FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28%); Q4 PAT INR 9.4 crore (+5.4%). Exchange holds about 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of spot market.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 issued 46 lakh I-RECs (+29% YoY); FY26 179 lakh (over +200%). Q4 revenue INR 2.2 crore; FY26 INR 7.7 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects electricity volume growth of 15-20% annually to continue in FY27, dependent on demand-supply conditions.
IGX gas volumes expected flat YoY in Q1 FY27 and to grow from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.
Coal exchange: draft Coal Regulations 2025 out; final regulations expected later in calendar 2026; board gave in-principle approval to explore setting up a coal exchange.
Management says market coupling would add no value and cost Grid India extra; IEX says it would absorb software changes at no extra cost.
Buyback under consideration; SEBI has not finalised the mechanism, and the company is awaiting SEBI's open-market route draft.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO process has been initiated; management says it is progressing well but did not give status detail.
PNGRB has given IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete the stake reduction.
Pending CERC approvals: TAM extension to 11 months, green RTM petition (reserved), and peak DAM/peak RTM segments for merchant storage (reserved).
BESS: 13 GW under first VGF tranche underway; about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded.
SECI 500 MW / 3-hour RE CfD pilot (1,500 MWh/day), backed by a INR 76 crore stabilisation fund; applies to battery capacity per management.
demand_pricing: DAM sell liquidity rose about 44% for FY26; FY26 DAM average INR 3.86/unit (down about 14%) and RTM INR 3.59/unit (down 16%).
More than 70% of cleared volume is now through the API system; management says over 5,000 industrial consumers use the platform.
Management says exchange customer count is rising and no customers have been lost to rival exchanges since the July 2025 coupling order.
Management sees the TAM segment (uniform liquidity across three exchanges) as evidence that transaction fees (about INR 0.036-0.037/unit) would hold up under coupling.
VPPA interest is currently limited, per management; data centres and multinationals could add demand later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about 29% versus the recent quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vineet Harlalka said the December quarter included a one-time treasury gain, and March saw mark-to-market losses from the Iran conflict and rupee weakness. He expects the numbers to recover as markets recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the final PMR and market coupling procedure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot estimate; PMR 2021 was notified in February 2021 after a 2019 draft, and the regulator will consider comments and market redesign.

qa_highlights.question: Would IEX lose volumes and margins if market coupling goes through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer loyalty and value-added services would retain share; cited TAM margins holding at about INR 0.036-0.037/unit despite shared liquidity. No additional software cost is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is RTM coupling feasible, given 48 auctions a day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management doubts RTM coupling is feasible: it would move from 48 to 288 five-minute blocks with no slack time, and an aggregation failure at one exchange could cause price jerks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the buyback stance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a buyback is a good option after the revised tax structure; the company is considering it and awaiting SEBI's open-market route decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will electricity volume growth continue in FY27 and why did REC volumes fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 15-20% volume growth. On RECs, management said there was no fall: REC volume rose 5% in FY26.

risks_watch: Market coupling: CERC draft (April 17, 2026) names Grid India as MCO; comments close May 16, 2026, and the timeline for final rules is unknown.
Gas exchange volumes weak in Q1 FY27 on Middle East supply disruption and high gas prices.
Treasury and other income volatility from mark-to-market swings (other income fell in Q4).
Continued DAM/RTM price decline (down 12-15% YoY in Q4) could pressure fee income if volumes do not offset.
Pending CERC approvals (TAM 11-month extension, green RTM, peak DAM/RTM) and the legal challenge to market coupling.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating volumes and the value of customer relationships, but evasive on market coupling timelines and outcomes, saying it was too early to call. Cautious on Q1 FY27 gas volumes and on the other income decline, which management attributed to non-recurring factors.
key_quotes: And I'm sure in the time to come, almost everybody will do the bidding through the API system.
So I have my own doubts about coupling in the RTM market.
We have more than 5,000 industrial consumers who are using with us.
Quantum in that is not significant. So the revenue share is not meaningful.

growth.why: Management guides electricity volume growth of 15-20% for FY27 (verbal, dependent on demand-supply), backed by demand gains (Q4 volume +24.3%, RTM +48%) but no specific capacity or contracts; IGX volume flat in Q1 FY27 and growth from Q2 if Middle East supply normalises.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: DAM price fell 12.2% and RTM 15% YoY in Q4 as sell-bids rose about 49%, and other income fell about 29% sequentially-adjusted, so fee pricing and treasury income are both pressured.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 15-20% electricity volume growth for FY27 after Q4 volume of 39.4 billion units (+24.3% YoY) and RTM +48.2%, though IGX is flat in Q1 FY27 on Middle East disruption.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Exchange is asset-light with no utilisation or capacity constraint discussed; the only capital moves are a buyback under consideration and an IGX IPO, not a capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Electricity volume guided at 15-20% growth for FY27 after Q4 volume rose 24.3% YoY, and IGX growth is expected from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: IGX volume is guided flat in Q1 FY27 after an 8% Q4 decline, and DAM/RTM prices fell 12.2%/15% YoY in Q4 while other income dropped sharply on March mark-to-market losses.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pending CERC approvals for green RTM and peak DAM/RTM segments (reserved) and a TAM 11-month extension could open new products, but timing depends on the regulator.

rows.label: Market coupling final rules (CERC draft names Grid India as MCO)
rows.why: CERC draft of April 17, 2026 has comments till May 16, but management cannot estimate the final timeline and PMR 2021 took about two years from draft to notification, so the outcome is a major overhang on volumes and fees.

rows.label: Buyback and IGX stake reduction/IPO
rows.why: Buyback is under consideration pending SEBI's open-market route draft, and PNGRB gave IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete its stake reduction, with the IPO process initiated.

rows.label: Coal exchange and BESS/RE storage demand
rows.why: Coal Regulations final rules are expected later in calendar 2026, and the 13 GW BESS first VGF tranche is underway with about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded, but no IEX contracts are quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes (Q4 +24.3%, RTM +48%) and customer retention, but evasive on market coupling timing and outcomes and cautious on Q1 FY27 gas volumes and the other income drop; analysts pressed on coupling and treasury income.
